A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AXIS and the same Microsoft Word studies. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original skill-exploration results, a 50-task comparison against UFO, and a 20-participant user study with performance and questionnaire outcomes in Sections 4–6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original skill-exploration results, 50-task comparison, and 20-participant user-study outcomes in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Both retain Follower/Explorer trajectory collection, monitoring, skill generation, API translation, and static/dynamic validation. V2 reorganizes this pipeline into three stages and documents exploration policies, validation inputs, and prompts more explicitly; these disclosures do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both use Microsoft Word on Windows, 347 exploration seed files, 50 feasibility tasks from WikiHow/Microsoft documentation, and the same five L1/L2 user-study tasks. No additional application, domain, population, or evaluated task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The feasibility comparison remains AXIS versus UFO as the UI Agent. The user study retains manual operation, UI Agent, and AXIS in the corresponding comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The user-study backend specification changes from GPT-4o, version 20240513, in v1 Section 5.4 to GPT-4, version 20240513, in v2 Section 6.1. This changes a reported setting, although v2's feasibility study still specifies GPT-4o and no rerun is established. The matched task counts, participants, metrics, and study procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the UI/API-action analysis, UI-agent failure explanations, and user-preference analysis. V2 reports no new ablation, robustness experiment, or diagnostic outcome. Its expanded validation instructions and highlighting-code example document the existing pipeline.

E5.justification: The pairwise significance entries and Figure 3 standard-error bars are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The reported skill counts, numerical comparisons, and user-study findings are retained. For example, v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 1 both report UFO/AXIS completion times of 59.5/29.9 seconds and success rates of 52%/84%. The corresponding user-study tables and Figures 3–4 also retain their results.

T1.justification: The NonEssential(N) criterion in v1 Section 7.1 is retained in v2 Appendix E.1. Skill nesting receives additional explanation, but no new mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain API-first HACI, automatic skill creation, reduced completion time and cognitive workload, and the application-as-agent/Agent OS vision. The abstract's quantitative claims are unchanged. The shorter title and conclusion and relocated UI-design discussion do not materially redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 Section 9 explicitly identifies dependence on Python-based APIs and limitations in exploration stability and efficiency. Appendix E.1 adds an explanation of controls that remain essential because they lack triggering APIs or are difficult to describe in language. Section 6.1 also corrects v1's statement that lower NASA-TLX scores indicate higher cognitive load.

D1.justification: V2 adds six agent prompt templates in Appendix F, concrete win32com/pywinauto executor information, worked generation/translation code in Table 8, and detailed exploration and validation instructions. Appendix D newly specifies numerical difficulty-classification thresholds. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's role-level descriptions, without establishing new experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds references connecting AXIS to tool making, Voyager-style skill learning, retrieval-augmented generation, API-based web agents, and large action models, while removing the standalone GPT-4V reference. These are limited additions to attribution and context; the main API-first HACI and Agent OS positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, methods, results, and conclusion are rewritten or condensed. V2 introduces a Preliminary section and three-stage method narrative, combines user-study methods and results, relocates detailed procedures and discussion to appendices, and adds Ethical Statement and Limitations sections.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document to two columns, redraws the framework and UI-pruning diagrams, adds the code-comparison Table 8, and extensively relocates and reformats existing displays. The login, manual-task, and questionnaire-transition screenshots are removed; result plots and the substantive survey forms are retained.

improvement.justification: The staged explanation, worked code, prompt appendix, and explicit task criteria make the existing work easier to understand and reproduce. Newly stated limitations better qualify its applicability. The empirical evidence is retained, and these documentation gains outweigh the small reproducibility regression introduced by inconsistent GPT-4/GPT-4o backend reporting.
